Team —

I pulled recent telemetry (see sample CSV attached: telemetry_sample.csv) for a mid-sized production account with a similar workload shape to what Aurelia described on the call (median request ~45 tokens, 95th ~210 tokens). Notes and proposed measurement methodology below — we should keep this language consistent in the questionnaire.

Proposed measurement methodology (engineer-friendly):
- Measurement window: calendar month UTC.
- Probing and sampling: continuous production sampling using edge-side request histograms (we ingest 100% of production requests, but for SLA reporting we apply a 1% deterministic sampling if the request volume > 10M tokens/day to bound storage; for typical enterprise volumes we'll use full sampling).
- Latency definition: server-side generation time (first-byte emit to final-byte-of-response). Client/network time excluded.
- Percentiles: p50/p95/p99 computed from the sampled set per 1-hour buckets and aggregated to the calendar month using weighted-percentile. We will publish both rolled-up global and region-specific numbers.
- Availability definition: percentage of 1-minute ingress windows in which the system returns an APPLICATION_RESPONSE (200/partial-200 with valid structured output) within the configured latency threshold. Acceptable transient errors (rate-limited responses) will be classified separately as throttling events and included in a throughput-normalized reconciliation.

Edge cases / caveats:
- Cold-starts for on-demand private deployments: for Private deployments we report availability after a 5-minute warmup window post-scale events. For Dedicated/hosted kept-warm pools the window is 30s.
- Model fallback: when a model variant is auto-failed-over, latency commitments apply to the served variant; we will surface the fallback event in the monthly telemetry but will not count fallback as an availability incident if thresholds met.

I'll add tighter wording for the questionnaire. Rafael — can you confirm commercial tolerance for a 99.95% baseline and the proposed credit bands? Laura — adding you for the credit language.

-Markus
Senior Reliability Engineer
Redwood Inference

From: Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.ai>

Subject: Re: SLA questionnaire: Redwood Inference - Aurelia RFP

All — attaching a draft of our completed questionnaire and a proposed service credit table (redwood_sla_response_20270328.pdf). Key commercial/legal notes to keep in mind for the Aurelia procurement team:

1) Baseline availability: 99.95% uptime measured monthly (per calendar month, UTC) for hosted and Dedicated environments. Private deployments require customer-side health probes; we provide the measurement harness and run hybrid validation for the first 60 days.

2) Latency SLOs (example commitments we can offer in the RFP):
   - Small model (LLM-small): p50 < 80ms, p95 < 180ms, p99 < 300ms (for payloads <= 64 tokens)
   - Medium model (LLM-medium): p50 < 120ms, p95 < 260ms, p99 < 420ms (payloads median 45 tokens)
   - Heavy/completion payloads will be scoped and listed separately.

3) Service credit table (monthly availability; credits as % of monthly fees):
   - >= 99.95%: 0% credit
   - 99.90% - 99.95%: 10% monthly service credit
   - 99.0% - 99.90%: 30% monthly service credit
   - < 99.0%: 60% monthly service credit + escalation credit review (possible one-time fee waiver)

4) Measurement & audit: credits issued after mutual review of telemetry. Customer may submit a dispute within 30 days of monthly report. We will provide raw sampled logs (redacted) for audit under NDA.

5) Exclusions: force majeure, scheduled maintenance with 72h notice, customer misconfiguration (network/DNS), and disruptions caused by third-party model providers; documented in questionnaire.

Rafael — the 99.95 baseline is what we usually propose for enterprise RFPs; please confirm if Aurelia asked for a stricter baseline on the call (I don't recall confirmation).

-Laury
Laura Bennett
Senior Counsel, Commercial
Redwood Inference

Subject: Final: Redwood SLA responses + telemetry sample for Aurelia RFP

Hi Claire / Michael —

Thanks for your patience. Attached is our completed SLA questionnaire and supporting telemetry sample. Summary of the key commitments in the attached PDF:

- Availability: 99.95% monthly uptime (calendar month, UTC) for hosted and Dedicated modes; Private deployment measurement supported with hybrid probes.
- Latency SLOs: example p50/p95/p99 bands included for small and medium models (see section 2 of the PDF).
- Measurement methodology: server-side generation-time percentiles computed from production sampling; 1-hour bucket aggregation; monthly weighted-percentile for p99. We include both global and region-specific reporting where region-specific traffic >= 1% of account volume.
- Service credits: proposed table (10% / 30% / 60% at the defined thresholds) with a 30-day dispute window and access to redacted sampled logs for audit under NDA.
- Operational caveats: cold-start warmup windows, fallback behavior, scheduled maintenance notice (>=72h for non-critical updates).

Next steps: please confirm receipt and whether you want the questionnaire returned in DocuSign for signature (we can generate a contract rider reflecting the SLA terms). If Aurelia wants a stricter availability floor (e.g., 99.99%), we can provide an addendum with pricing impact and Dedicated-reserved sizing to meet that target.

We look forward to your feedback.
